title: Selling Plans Refund Frequency Multiplier on Administration Fees
content:
Sellers who fund refunds often pay a higher administration fee on a **Selling Plans** refund credit. The count is taken from the seller-funded refund debits on the seller's Northloop Payments account, on any order.

**Rule.** The refund administration fee is multiplied by the frequent-refund multiplier when the payments account shows at least the frequent-refund count of seller-funded refund debits dated less than three whole months before the decision date, by the repeat-refund multiplier when it shows at least the repeat-refund count but fewer than the frequent-refund count, and by one when it shows fewer.

The multiplier applies to the refund administration fee as worked out from the credit before the fee and its rate; the product is then rounded to the nearest cent, and only the rounded amount is compared with the cap.

| Seller-funded refund debits dated less than three whole months before the decision date | Multiplier on the refund administration fee |
|---|---|
| 4 or more (the frequent-refund count) | 1.5 (frequent-refund multiplier) |
| 2 or 3 (at least the repeat-refund count, fewer than 4) | 1.25 (repeat-refund multiplier) |
| 0 or 1 | One |

## Which debits are counted (hypothetical decision on 20 July)

- A seller-funded refund debit dated 21 April is less than three whole months before 20 July and is counted.
- A debit dated 20 April is a full three whole months before 20 July and is not counted.

## Applying it (hypothetical)

A credit before the fee of USD 12.00 at a rate of 20% gives USD 2.40. With 4 seller-funded refund debits dated less than three whole months before the decision date the multiplier is 1.5 and the fee is USD 3.60; with 2 debits it is 1.25 and the fee is USD 3.00; with 1 debit it stays USD 2.40. Each figure is then compared with the cap.
